Figure caption: Storage buffer screening against freeze–thaw for F1–F5 Fluc mRNA–LNP formulations, including (a,b) particle size, (c,d) polydispersity index, (e,f) encapsulation efficiency, and (g,h) in vitro transfection efficiency in HEK-293 cells. All data are mean ± SD (n ≥ 3). F—Formulation; FLuc—Firefly luciferase; mRNA–LNP—Messenger ribonucleic acid–lipid nanoparticle; PBS—Phosphate-Buffered Saline; n—Number of samples; SD—Standard deviation.

Figure caption: Cryo-TEM images of F1–F4 mRNA–LNPs scanned at day one and after 12 months stored at different temperatures. The scale bars show 100 nm for all the images. Cryo-TEM—Cryogenic transmission electron microscopy; F—Formulation; mRNA–LNP—Messenger ribonucleic acid–lipid nanoparticle.

Figure caption: Long-term physicochemical stability of FLuc mRNA–LNPs (F1–F4) in 20 mM and 30 mM Tris with 10% sucrose. Hydrodynamic diameter (z-average particle size distribution) measured by DLS at 0, 0.5, 1, 3, 6, and 12 months under four storage temperatures (−80 °C, −20 °C, 5 °C, 25 °C). Encapsulation efficiency determined by RiboGreen assay. All data are mean ± SD (n ≥ 3). No statistical significance was observed between 20 mM and 30 mM Tris corresponding samples (One-way ANOVA, p-value > 0.05). DLS—Dynamic light scattering; EE—Encapsulation efficiency; F—Formulation; FLuc—Firefly luciferase; mRNA–LNP—Messenger ribonucleic acid–lipid nanoparticle; n—Number of samples; SD—Standard deviation.

Figure caption: Effect of storage temperature and buffer strength on subvisible particle concentration of FLuc mRNA–LNPs. The graphs show subvisible particle counts (≥10 µm and ≥25 µm) by MFI after 12 months. Graphs represent four formulations (F1–F4) in 20 mM (left panel) or 30 mM (right panel) Tris + 10% sucrose stored at −80 °C, −20 °C, 5 °C, or 25 °C. Data are mean of two repeated measures. F—Formulation; FLuc—Firefly luciferase; MFI—Micro-Flow™ Imaging; mRNA–LNP—Messenger ribonucleic acid–lipid nanoparticle.

Figure caption: Oxidized or hydrolyzed lipid content of LNPs stored in different buffers for 12 months at various storage temperatures and measured by LC-MS. The LC-MS peak areas of three main lipid species, including DSPC-C18H34O, MC3 N-oxide, and ALC-0315 + [O], of LNPs in four formulations (F1, F2, F3, and F4) are summarized in the graphs. The data are presented as the fold normalized to the corresponding −80 °C condition. The dashed line indicates a peak area ratio of one. All data are mean ± SD (n = 3 repeated measures). F—Formulation; LC-MS—Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry; LNP—Lipid nanoparticle; n—Number of samples; SD—Standard deviation.

Figure caption: mRNA purity % and in vitro transfection efficiency of FLuc mRNA–LNPs (F1–F4) in 20 mM and 30 mM Tris + 10% sucrose. Samples were measured at 0, 0.5, 1, 3, 6, and 12 months under four storage temperatures (−80 °C, −20 °C, 5 °C, 25 °C). mRNA purity % was measured by MCE. Transfection efficiency was performed on HEK-293 cells, and the luciferase intensity was measured at 24 h post-treatment. For transfection, the data are mean ± SD (n ≥ 3). At 12-month timepoints, no statistical significance was observed between 20 mM and 30 mM Tris corresponding samples in transfection efficiency results. (One-way ANOVA, p-value > 0.05). For mRNA purity, the data are the means of 3 repeated measures. Note: the time-zero FLuc mRNA purity is <100% due to inherent in vitro transcribed mRNA drug substance heterogeneity and drug substance handling (one freeze–thaw cycle) prior to LNP preparation. F—Formulation; FLuc—Firefly luciferase; LNP—Lipid nanoparticles; MCE—Microchip capillary electrophoresis; MLI—Mean luminescence intensity; mRNA—Messenger ribonucleic acid; SD—Standard deviation.

Figure caption: In vivo transfection efficiency of FLuc mRNA–LNPs at Day 1 and after 12 months of storage at 30 mM Tris. (a) Representative IVIS® images 24 h post-injection (5 µg kg−1) of formulations F1–F4 stored at −80 °C (dark blue symbols), −20 °C (light blue symbols), 5 °C (green symbols), or 25 °C (red symbols) at 30 mM Tris and 10% sucrose formulation. (b) Quantified whole-body luminescence (total flux) relative to day one baseline. (c) Quantified liver (upper graph) and spleen (lower graph) luminescence after 12 months storage at different temperatures compared to freshly prepared F1 LNPs. Bars represent mean ± SEM (n = 4). ns: statistically not significant (One-way ANOVA, p-value = 0.73). F—Formulation; FLuc—Firefly luciferase; mRNA–LNP—Messenger ribonucleic acid–lipid nanoparticle; n = Number of animals; SEM—Standard error of the mean.

Table caption: Lipid composition of formulated FLuc mRNA–LNPs.

Table caption: Quality attributes (QAs) and associated analytical techniques/assays used to assess the FLuc mRNA–LNP drug product quality.

Table caption: mRNA 5′-capping integrity at 12 months of different LNP formulations stored at various temperatures. Data are the mean of three repeated measures. F—Formulation; LNP—Lipid nanoparticle; mRNA—Messenger ribonucleic acid; N.D.—Not determined due to the extensive mRNA degradation or sample issues; * Threshold at 100%.
